newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Heavy fighting in Sierra Leone capital.
newsitem.headline: Heavy fighting in Sierra Leone capital.

text.p: Heavy shooting erupted in the Sierra Leone capital Freetown on Sunday and a military spokesman went on state radio to order political leaders to report to army headquarters.
The spokesman, who identified himself as Corporal Gborie, said the fighting was an internal matter and ordered Nigerian and Guinean troops stationed in Sierra Leone to keep out.
He condemned the government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, saying: "We want democracy but not this democracy. Our soldiers have been suffering for far too long."

Heavy gunfire broke out soon after 5 a.m. (0500 GMT) from the direction of the government offices at State House and the military headquarters, with troops using automatic machineguns, mortars and rocket-propelled grenades.
"All ministers and other politicians should immediately report to military headquarters," the spokesman said.
The shooting continued through the morning, with the attacks apparently meeting some resistance.
Soldiers patrolling the streets wore red ceremonial uniforms instead of their usual green fatigues.
Witnesses said about 20 heavily armed soldiers broke into the Pademba Road central prison in the capital and freed more than 600 inmates.
A helicopter landed and took off from Kabbah's Freetown home but it was not immediately clear whether he was aboard.

The army has shown growing signs of discontent with troop reductions specified under a peace agreement with rebels of the Revolutionary United Front and there has been tension between southern Mendes who back Kabbah's Sierra Leone Peoples Party and northern tribes who feel marginalised by his government.
A series of recent lightning attacks in the north have been officially blamed on the rebels, who signed a peace accord with Kabbah in November, but the army was widely rumoured to be involved.
